verses.tafsirV2: (And Allah, all unseen, surroundeth them) He says: He is Aware of them and of their works.

verses.text: بَلۡ هُوَ قُرۡءَانٞ مَّجِيدٞ
verses.translation: But this is an honored Qur'an
verses.tafsir: Nay but it is a glorious a magnificent Qur’ān
verses.tafsirV2: (Nay, but it) i.e. the Qur'an which Muhammad (pbuh) recites to you (is a glorious Qur'an) is a noble and honoured Qur'an

verses.text: فِي لَوۡحٖ مَّحۡفُوظِۭ
verses.translation: [Inscribed] in a Preserved Slate
verses.tafsir: in a tablet suspended above the seventh heaven preserved read mahfūzin from all devils and from having any of its contents altered; it is a high as the distance between the earth and the heaven and as wide as the distance between the east and the west made of white pearls — as stated by Ibn ‘Abbās may God be pleased with both him and his father ‘Abbās
verses.tafsirV2: (On a guarded tablet) He says: it is written on a tablet that is protected from the devils'.

verses.text: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلطَّارِقِ
verses.translation: By the sky and the night comer
verses.tafsir: By the heaven and the night-visitor! al-tāriq actually denotes any thing that comes by night including stars because they come out at night.
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the heaven and the Morning Star): '(By the heaven and the Morning Star) He says: Allah swears by the heaven and the morning star

verses.text: وَمَآ أَدۡرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلطَّارِقُ
verses.translation: And what can make you know what is the night comer
verses.tafsir: And what will tell you what the night-visitor is? mā’l-tāriq is a subject and predicate standing as the second object of the verb adrā ‘tell’; and what comes after the first mā ‘what’ is the predicate thereof of this first mā — this statement emphasises the magnificence of the ‘night-visitor’ which is explained in what follows. It is
verses.tafsirV2: (Ah, what will tell thee) O Muhammad (what the Morning Star is!) this is to arouse his astonishment.

verses.text: ٱلنَّجۡمُ ٱلثَّاقِبُ
verses.translation: It is the piercing star
verses.tafsir: The piercing the brilliant because of its piercing the darkness with its light star! meaning the constellation Pleiades; or it refers to all stars the response to the oath follows
verses.tafsirV2: Allah then explained by saying: (The piercing Star!) the bright, piercing star; this refers to the planet Saturn which shines at night and disappears during the day.

verses.text: إِن كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ لَّمَّا عَلَيۡهَا حَافِظٞ
verses.translation: There is no soul but that it has over it a protector
verses.tafsir: Over every soul there is a keeper if read la-mā then mā is extra and in is softened in place of the hardened form with its subject omitted that is to say innahu; the lām is a particle for separation; if read lammā then in is for negation and lammā means illā ‘except that’ — the watcher is an angel that keeps a record of its deeds both the good and the evil.
verses.tafsirV2: (No human soul) no believing or disbelieving soul-this is why Allah swore-(but hath a guardian over it) who record its words and deeds until he drives it into the grave.

verses.text: فَلۡيَنظُرِ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ
verses.translation: So let man observe from what he was created
verses.tafsir: So let man consider by way of reflection from what he was created from what thing
verses.tafsirV2: (So let man) Abu Talib (consider from what he is created) from what his soul is created.

verses.text: خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٖ دَافِقٖ
verses.translation: He was created from a fluid, ejected
verses.tafsir: the response is He was created from a gushing fluid gushing forth from the man and the woman into the womb
verses.tafsirV2: Allah then explained, saying: (He is created from a gushing fluid) into the womb of a woman

verses.text: يَخۡرُجُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ ٱلصُّلۡبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ
verses.translation: Emerging from between the backbone and the ribs
verses.tafsir: issuing from between the loins of the man and the breast-bones of the woman.
verses.tafsirV2: (That issued from between the loins) of a man (and ribs) the ribs of a woman.

verses.text: إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجۡعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٞ
verses.translation: Indeed, Allah, to return him [to life], is Able
verses.tafsir: Assuredly He exalted be He is able to bring him back to resurrect man after his death; and so when he reflects on his origins he will realise that the One who was able to do this is also able to resurrect him
verses.tafsirV2: (Lo! He) i.e. Allah (verily is Able to return him (unto life)) He is able to return that fluid from whence it came and He is Able to bring him back after death and revive him.

verses.text: يَوۡمَ تُبۡلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ
verses.translation: The Day when secrets will be put on trial
verses.tafsir: on the day when all secrets the hidden convictions and intentions of the hearts are inspected when they are examined and revealed
verses.tafsirV2: (On the day when hidden thoughts shall be searched out) when all the secrets that a person knows, and no one else other than him knows, become manifest.

verses.text: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٖ وَلَا نَاصِرٖ
verses.translation: Then man will have no power or any helper
verses.tafsir: whereat he the one who denies resurrection will have neither strength to defend himself against chastisement nor any helper to avert it from him.
verses.tafsirV2: (Then will he) Abu Talib (have no might) to defend himself (nor any helper) to shield him from Allah's chastisement.

verses.text: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلرَّجۡعِ
verses.translation: By the sky which returns [rain]
verses.tafsir: By the heaven of returns of the rain that returns time and again
verses.tafsirV2: (By the heaven which giveth the returning rain) Allah swore by the heaven which accumulates clouds after cloud, year after year,

verses.text: وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدۡعِ
verses.translation: And [by] the earth which cracks open
verses.tafsir: and by the earth of fissures splitting with the growth of vegetation
verses.tafsirV2: (And the earth which splitteth (with the growth of trees and plants)) and it is also said this means: and by the earth which has firm pillars

verses.text: إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوۡلٞ فَصۡلٞ
verses.translation: Indeed, the Qur'an is a decisive statement
verses.tafsir: assuredly it the Qur’ān is a decisive word distinguishing between truth and falsehood
verses.tafsirV2: This is the reason why Allah swore: (Lo! this (Qur'an) is a conclusive word) a true exposition; it is also said this means: it is a judgement from Allah,

verses.text: وَمَا هُوَ بِٱلۡهَزۡلِ
verses.translation: And it is not amusement
verses.tafsir: and it is not a jest frivolity or falsehood.
verses.tafsirV2: (It is no pleasantry) it is no falsehood.

verses.text: إِنَّهُمۡ يَكِيدُونَ كَيۡدٗا
verses.translation: Indeed, they are planning a plan
verses.tafsir: Indeed they that is the disbelievers are devising a plot they are preparing plots against the Prophet s
verses.tafsirV2: (Lo! They) i.e. the people of Mecca (plot a plot (against thee, O Muhammad)) they scheme in their state of disbelief, that is to say they bar people from Muhammad (pbuh) and from the Qur'an; it is also said this means: they plan, in Dar al-Nadwah, to kill you, O Muhammad!

verses.text: وَأَكِيدُ كَيۡدٗا
verses.translation: But I am planning a plan
verses.tafsir: and I too am devising a plot drawing them by degrees towards destruction from whence they know not.
verses.tafsirV2: (And I plot a plot (against them)) and I want to kill them, O Muhammad, on the Day of Badr.

verses.text: فَمَهِّلِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ أَمۡهِلۡهُمۡ رُوَيۡدَۢا
verses.translation: So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile
verses.tafsir: So respite O Muhammad (s) the disbelievers; grant them respite reiterated as an emphasis one enhanced by the use of a different form mahhil amhil that is to say put them off for a little ruwaydā is a verbal noun emphasising the import of the operator and is the diminutive form of rūd or irwad with shortening of final consonant ruwaydan ruwaydā. Surely enough God exalted be He seized them at Badr and abrogated the dispensation of ‘granting respite’ by the ‘sword’ verse in other words by the command to fight and struggle.
verses.tafsirV2: (So give a respite to the disbelievers. Deal thou gently with them for a while) give them a while until the Day of Badr'.

verses.text: سَبِّحِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَى
verses.translation: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High
verses.tafsir: Glorify the Name of your Lord that is exalt your Lord above what does not befit Him ism in isma rabbika ‘the Name of your Lord’ is extra the Most High an adjective qualifying rabbika ‘your Lord’
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (Praise the name of thy Lord the Most High): '(Praise the name of your Lord the Most High) He says: pray, O Muhammad, by the command of your Lord the Most High, Who is Higher than all things; it is also said that this means: remember, O Muhammad, the divine Oneness of your Lord; and it is said this means: say, O Muhammad, in your prostration “praise be to my Lord the Most High”,

verses.text: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ
verses.translation: Who created and proportioned
verses.tafsir: Who created and proportioned His creature making it of well-proportioned parts without irregularities
verses.tafsirV2: (Who createth) every thing that has a soul, (then disposeth) He created them with two hands, two feet, two eyes, two ears and with other organs too;

verses.text: وَٱلَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ
verses.translation: And who destined and [then] guided
verses.tafsir: and Who determined what He wants and guided to what He had determined of good or evil
verses.tafsirV2: (Who measureth) He made every male and female, (then guideth) then He made known and inspired how the male and female come; it is also said this means: He measured a person's creation, thus making him handsome or ugly, tall or short; it is also said this means: He measured felicity and wretchedness for His created beings, and so He made plain disbelief and faith, good and evil;

verses.text: وَٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلۡمَرۡعَىٰ
verses.translation: And who brings out the pasture
verses.tafsir: and Who brought forth the pasture Who caused herbage to grow
verses.tafsirV2: (Who bringeth forth the pasturage) green pasture by means of the rain,

verses.text: فَجَعَلَهُۥ غُثَآءً أَحۡوَىٰ
verses.translation: And [then] makes it black stubble
verses.tafsir: then made it after verdancy blackened stubble desiccated broken chaff.
verses.tafsirV2: (Then turneth it) after being green (to russet stubble) i.e. He makes it dry and black when it exceeds a year.

verses.text: سَنُقۡرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰٓ
verses.translation: We will make you recite, [O Muhammad], and you will not forget
verses.tafsir: We will have you recite the Qur’ān so that you will not forget what you recite
verses.tafsirV2: (We shall make thee read (O Muhammad)) We shall teach, O Muhammad, the Qur'an; it is also said this means: Gabriel shall read to you the Qur'an (so that thou shalt not forget

verses.text: إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّهُۥ يَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡجَهۡرَ وَمَا يَخۡفَىٰ
verses.translation: Except what Allah should will. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden
verses.tafsir: except what God may will that you forget by abrogating its recitation and its ruling — the Prophet s used to recite aloud while Gabriel recited fearing to forget and so it is as though it was said to him ‘Do not hasten in it; you will not forget and so do not weary yourself by reciting it aloud’; assuredly He exalted be He knows what is overt of words and deeds and what is hidden of both of these.
verses.tafsirV2: Save that which Allah willeth) and Allah willed that you do not forget; and the Prophet (pbuh) never forgot a bit of the Qur'an after this. (Lo! He knoweth the disclosed) He knows the works that are done and the words that are said in the open (and that which still is hidden) of secrets which you have thought about in yourself;

verses.text: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلۡيُسۡرَىٰ
verses.translation: And We will ease you toward ease
verses.tafsir: And We will ease your way to the easy way the uncomplicated Law namely Islam.
verses.tafsirV2: (And We shall ease thy way unto the state of ease) We shall make easy for you the conveyance of the message and all other acts of obedience.

verses.text: فَذَكِّرۡ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
verses.translation: So remind, if the reminder should benefit
verses.tafsir: So remind admonish by the Qur’ān in case the reminder should be of benefit to the one whom you might remind the one mentioned in the following verse ‘he who fears will be reminded’ in other words even if it might not be of benefit for it is of benefit to some but of no benefit to others.
verses.tafsirV2: (Therefore remind (men)) admonish by means of the Qur'an and through Allah, (for of use is the reminder) He says: admonition by means of the Qur'an and through Allah does not benefit except he who fears Allah, i.e. the believer.

verses.text: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخۡشَىٰ
verses.translation: He who fears [Allah] will be reminded
verses.tafsir: He who fears God exalted be He will be reminded by it as in the verse So admonish by the Qur’ān him who fears My threat Q. 5045;
verses.tafsirV2: (He will heed) he will take admonition by means of the Qur'an and through Allah (who feareth) Allah, i.e. the Muslim,

verses.text: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلۡأَشۡقَى
verses.translation: But the wretched one will avoid it
verses.tafsir: but the wretched one al-ashqā means al-shaqī that is to say the disbeliever will shun it that is the reminder in other words he will leave it aside not looking at it
verses.tafsirV2: (But the most hapless) the damned, as it is in Allah's foreknowledge, (will flout it) will steer away and avoid taking admonition by means of the Qur'an or through Allah,

verses.text: ٱلَّذِي يَصۡلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلۡكُبۡرَىٰ
verses.translation: [He] who will [enter and] burn in the greatest Fire
verses.tafsir: he who will be roasted in the greater Fire the Fire of the Hereafter the lesser fire being that of this world;
verses.tafsirV2: (He who will be flung to the great fire) he who will enter the Fire in the Hereafter, and there is no chastisement greater than the Fire

verses.text: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحۡيَىٰ
verses.translation: Neither dying therein nor living
verses.tafsir: then he will neither die therein and find rest nor live a enjoyable life.
verses.tafsirV2: (Wherein) in the Fire (he will neither die) and thus be put out of his misery (nor live) a beneficial life.

verses.text: قَدۡ أَفۡلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
verses.translation: He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself
verses.tafsir: Successful winner indeed is he who purifies himself who cleanses himself by means of his adherence to faith
verses.tafsirV2: (He is successful) and saved (who groweth) he who takes admonition by means of the Qur'an and believes in Allah's divine Oneness,

verses.text: وَذَكَرَ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ
verses.translation: And mentions the name of his Lord and prays
verses.tafsir: and mentions the Name of his Lord saying Allāhu akbar ‘God is Great’ and prays the five prayers — and such are the concerns of one working towards the Hereafter concerns which the Meccan disbelievers shun.
verses.tafsirV2: (And remembereth the name) the command (of his Lord) regarding the five daily prayers and other things, (so prayeth) the five daily prayers in congregation; this verse can also be understood to mean: he is successful and saved he who gives the charity of Fitr before going out to pray and mentions the name of his Lord saying " there is no deity save Allah " and upon going to prayer and returning from it says " Allah is the Most Great " and then prays the 'Id prayer with the Imam.

verses.text: بَلۡ تُؤۡثِرُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا
verses.translation: But you prefer the worldly life
verses.tafsir: Nay but you prefer or read yu’thirūna ‘they prefer’ the life of this world to the Hereafter
verses.tafsirV2: But ye prefer the life of the world) you chose to strive for the life of the world and preferred the reward of the life of the world to the reward of the Hereafter.

verses.text: وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرٞ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓ
verses.translation: While the Hereafter is better and more enduring
verses.tafsir: whereas the Hereafter and the Paradise it entails is better and more lasting.
verses.tafsirV2: (Although the Hereafter) striving for the Hereafter and the reward of the Hereafter (is better) than striving for the life of the world and reward of the life of the world (and more lasting.

verses.text: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَفِي ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ
verses.translation: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures
verses.tafsir: Truly this the success of those who purify themselves and the Hereafter being better is in the former scrolls the ones revealed before the Qur’ān
verses.tafsirV2: Lo! This) from His saying: (He is Successful) up to here (is in the former scrolls) in the Scriptures of the people of old,

verses.text: صُحُفِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ
verses.translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses
verses.tafsir: the scrolls of Abraham and Moses the ten scrolls of Abraham and the Torah of Moses.
verses.tafsirV2: (The Book of Abraham and Moses) the Scripture of Moses is the Torah and only Allah knows about the Scripture of Abraham'.

verses.text: هَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ٱلۡغَٰشِيَةِ
verses.translation: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming [event]
verses.tafsir: Has there — there has indeed — come to you the tiding of the Enveloper? the Resurrection so called because it ‘envelops’ creatures with its terrors.
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (Hath there come unto you): '(Hath there come unto you) He says: it has not come unto you, O Muhammad, before but now it has; it is also said that this means: it has come unto you (tidings of the Overwhelming) the news of the coming of the Hour? It is also said the Overwhelming refers to the Fire overwhelming its dwellers.

verses.text: وُجُوهٞ يَوۡمَئِذٍ خَٰشِعَةٌ
verses.translation: [Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled
verses.tafsir: Some faces on that day — they faces are used to represent the individuals in both instances — will be humbled abject
verses.tafsirV2: (On that day) the Day of Judgement ((many) faces) the faces of the disbelievers and hypocrites (will be downcast) abased because of the chastisement,

verses.text: عَامِلَةٞ نَّاصِبَةٞ
verses.translation: Working [hard] and exhausted
verses.tafsir: toiling weary tired and exhausted from the chains and fetters
verses.tafsirV2: (Toiling) dragged in the Fire, (weary) in tiredness and strife; it is also said this means: toiling in the life of the world, weary in the Hereafter, this refers to the Christian monks and anchorites, and it is also said it refers to the Kharijites.

verses.text: تَصۡلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةٗ
verses.translation: They will [enter to] burn in an intensely hot Fire
verses.tafsir: roasting read taslā or tuslā in a scorching fire
verses.tafsirV2: (Scorched by burning fire) they enter the Fire whose heat is extreme,

verses.text: تُسۡقَىٰ مِنۡ عَيۡنٍ ءَانِيَةٖ
verses.translation: They will be given drink from a boiling spring
verses.tafsir: made to drink from a boiling spring one of extremely hot temperatures.
verses.tafsirV2: (Drinking) in the Fire (from a boiling spring),

verses.text: لَّيۡسَ لَهُمۡ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِن ضَرِيعٖ
verses.translation: For them there will be no food except from a poisonous, thorny plant
verses.tafsir: They will have no food except cactus darī‘ — a type of thorn plant which no animal grazes on because of its vileness —
verses.tafsirV2: (No food for them) in those abysmal pits (save bitter thorn fruit) the shabraq plant which grows in the roads of Mecca, which is eaten by camels when it is soft but when it is hard it becomes like the claws of cats.

verses.text: لَّا يُسۡمِنُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي مِن جُوعٖ
verses.translation: Which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger
verses.tafsir: neither nourishing nor availing against hunger.
verses.tafsirV2: (Which doth not nourish nor release from hunger) when one eats it.

verses.text: وُجُوهٞ يَوۡمَئِذٖ نَّاعِمَةٞ
verses.translation: [Other] faces, that Day, will show pleasure
verses.tafsir: Other faces on that day will be delicate fair
verses.tafsirV2: (In that day other faces) the faces of true believers (will be calm) beautiful and radiant,

verses.text: لِّسَعۡيِهَا رَاضِيَةٞ
verses.translation: With their effort [they are] satisfied
verses.tafsir: pleased by their efforts in the life of the world expended in obedience pleased in the Hereafter upon seeing the reward thereof;
verses.tafsirV2: (Glad for their effort past) He says: they are pleased with the reward of their works,

verses.text: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٖ
verses.translation: In an elevated garden
verses.tafsir: in a lofty Garden lofty in a physical as well as an abstract sense
verses.tafsirV2: (In a high Garden) in a high rank

verses.text: لَّا تَسۡمَعُ فِيهَا لَٰغِيَةٗ
verses.translation: Wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech
verses.tafsir: in which they will not hear read lā yusma‘u ‘will not be heard’ or lā tasma‘u ‘they will not hear’ any vanity any inane soul speaking drivel;
verses.tafsirV2: (Where) in Paradise (they hear no idle speech) any oath whether it is true or false,

verses.text: فِيهَا عَيۡنٞ جَارِيَةٞ
verses.translation: Within it is a flowing spring
verses.tafsir: therein is a running spring of water meaning ‘springs’;
verses.tafsirV2: (Wherein) in Paradise (is a gushing spring) gushing with goodness, grace and mercy for them,

verses.text: فِيهَا سُرُرٞ مَّرۡفُوعَةٞ
verses.translation: Within it are couches raised high
verses.tafsir: therein are lofty couches lofty in terms of their essence their size and physical location
verses.tafsirV2: (Wherein) in Paradise (are couches raised) in the air for as long as its owners are away; it is also said that they are raised for its people.

verses.text: وَأَكۡوَابٞ مَّوۡضُوعَةٞ
verses.translation: And cups put in place
verses.tafsir: and goblets vessels without handles set around the edges of the springs prepared for them to drink with
verses.tafsirV2: (And goblets) round goblets that do not have handles, ears or nooses (set at hand) in their dwellings.

verses.text: وَنَمَارِقُ مَصۡفُوفَةٞ
verses.translation: And cushions lined up
verses.tafsir: and cushions arrayed one next to the other against which they may lean
verses.tafsirV2: (And cushions ranged) against each other.

verses.text: وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبۡثُوثَةٌ
verses.translation: And carpets spread around
verses.tafsir: and carpets rugs of velvet-hair spread out.
verses.tafsirV2: (And silken carpets spread) for its owners.

verses.text: أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡإِبِلِ كَيۡفَ خُلِقَتۡ
verses.translation: Then do they not look at the camels - how they are created
verses.tafsir: Will they the Meccan disbelievers not consider by way of reflection the camels how they are created?
verses.tafsirV2: When the Prophet (pbuh) informed them of this, the disbelievers of Mecca said: " Bring us a sign to prove that Allah has sent you to us as a Messenger ". Therefore Allah said: (Will they not regard the camels, how they are created) with their strength and power, carrying burdens that no one else can carry?

verses.text: وَإِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيۡفَ رُفِعَتۡ
verses.translation: And at the sky - how it is raised
verses.tafsir: And the heaven how it was raised?
verses.tafsirV2: (And the heaven, how it is raised) how it is raised above creation, and no one can touch it?

verses.text: وَإِلَى ٱلۡجِبَالِ كَيۡفَ نُصِبَتۡ
verses.translation: And at the mountains - how they are erected
verses.tafsir: And the mountains how they were set?
verses.tafsirV2: (And the hills, how they are set up) on earth, unmoved?

verses.text: وَإِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَيۡفَ سُطِحَتۡ
verses.translation: And at the earth - how it is spread out
verses.tafsir: And the earth how it was laid out flat? and thus infer from this the power of God exalted be He and His Oneness? The commencing with the mention of camels is because they are closer in contact with it the earth than any other animal. As for His words sutihat ‘laid out flat’ this on a literal reading suggests that the earth is flat which is the opinion of most of the scholars of the revealed Law and not a sphere as astronomers ahl al-hay’a have it even if this latter does not contradict any of the pillars of the Law.
verses.tafsirV2: (And the earth, how it is spread) over water? All these are signs for them.

verses.text: فَذَكِّرۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٞ
verses.translation: So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are only a reminder
verses.tafsir: So remind them of God’s graces and the proofs affirming His Oneness. For you are only an admonisher;
verses.tafsirV2: (Remind them) admonish them, (for thou art but a remembrancer) you are but a warner by means of the Qur'an; it is also said that this means: you are only an admonisher by the Qur'an and through Allah,

verses.text: لَّسۡتَ عَلَيۡهِم بِمُصَيۡطِرٍ
verses.translation: You are not over them a controller
verses.tafsir: you are not a taskmaster over them a variant reading for musaytir has musaytir that is to say not one who has been given authority over them — this was revealed before the command to struggle against the disbelievers.
verses.tafsirV2: (Thou art not) O Muhammad (at all a warder over them) you are not imposed on them such that you force them to accept faith.

verses.text: إِلَّا مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ
verses.translation: However, he who turns away and disbelieves
verses.tafsir: But he who turns away he who rejects faith and disbelieves in the Qur’ān
verses.tafsirV2: Later on, Allah commanded him to fight them, saying: (But whoso is averse and disbelieveth) except he who turns away from faith and disbelieves in Allah,

verses.text: فَيُعَذِّبُهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرَ
verses.translation: Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment
verses.tafsir: God will chastise him with the greater chastisement the chastisement of the Hereafter the lesser chastisement being that of this world that of being killed or taken captive.
verses.tafsirV2: (Allah will punish him) in the Hereafter (with direst punishment) i.e. with the punishment of the Fire.

verses.text: إِنَّ إِلَيۡنَآ إِيَابَهُمۡ
verses.translation: Indeed, to Us is their return
verses.tafsir: Truly to Us will be their return their coming back after death
verses.tafsirV2: (Lo! unto Us is their return) in the Hereafter.

verses.text: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيۡنَا حِسَابَهُم
verses.translation: Then indeed, upon Us is their account
verses.tafsir: then truly with Us will lie their reckoning their requital which We will never abandon.
verses.tafsirV2: (And Ours their reckoning) their steadfastness in the life of the world and reward and punishment in the Hereafter'.

verses.text: وَٱلۡفَجۡرِ
verses.translation: By the dawn
verses.tafsir: By the dawn that is to say by the dawn of each day
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the Dawn): '(By the Dawn) He says: He swears by the dawn which is the breaking of day; it is also said it is the whole day; and it is also said that this refers to the dawn of the year.

verses.text: وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٖ
verses.translation: And [by] ten nights
verses.tafsir: and by the ten nights the first ten nights of Dhū’l-Hijja
verses.tafsirV2: (And ten nights) the first ten nights of Dhu'l-Hijjah,

verses.text: وَٱلشَّفۡعِ وَٱلۡوَتۡرِ
verses.translation: And [by] the even [number] and the odd
verses.tafsir: and by the even the pair and the odd read watr or witr two alternative forms the single
verses.tafsirV2: (And the Even) the day of 'Arafah and the day of immolation (and the Odd) three days after the day of immolation; it is also said that the Even refers to all prayers which are made of an even number of units: two or four units of prayer-the Subh, Zuhr, 'Asr and 'Isha' prayers-while the Odd refers to the prayers which consists of an odd number of units of prayer such as the Maghrib and Witr prayers; it is also said that the Even refers to Heaven and earth, the life of the world and the Hereafter, Paradise and hell, the Throne and the Stool, the sun and the moon, while the Odd refers to everything that is odd in number; it is also said that the Even refers to the male and female, disbeliever and believer, the sincere and hypocrite, the righteous and the sinful, while the Odd refers to Allah.

verses.text: وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَسۡرِ
verses.translation: And [by] the night when it passes
verses.tafsir: and by the night in motion falling or receding
verses.tafsirV2: (And the night when it departeth) this refers to the night of Muzdalifah; it is also said this means: the night in which people come and go; Allah swore by all these things that: your Lord, O Muhammad, is ever Watchful. He says:

verses.text: هَلۡ فِي ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٞ لِّذِي حِجۡرٍ
verses.translation: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception
verses.tafsir: Is there in that oath an oath for one of sense? one of intellect the response to the oath has been omitted that is to say it is to be understood as something like la-tu‘adhdhabunna yā kuffāra Makka ‘you will assuredly be chastised O disbelievers of Mecca!’.
verses.tafsirV2: (There) in that which I have mentioned (surely is an oath for thinking man.

verses.text: أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
verses.translation: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad
verses.tafsir: Have you not seen do you not know O Muhammad (s) how your Lord dealt with ‘Ād
verses.tafsirV2: Dost thou not consider) have you not been informed, O Muhammad, in the Qur'an (how thy Lord dealt with (the tribe of) 'Aad) the people of Hud, how Allah, Exalted is He, destroyed them when they disbelieved,

verses.text: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلۡعِمَادِ
verses.translation: [With] Iram - who had lofty pillars
verses.tafsir: Iram — these were the former people of ‘Ād Irama is an explicative supplement or a substitution and it is treated as a diptote because it is a proper noun and feminine — of the towering ones that is to say the tall ones — the tallest one among them would reach four hundred cubits —
verses.tafsirV2: (With many columned) powerful (Iram) the son of Iram; Iram is Shem son of Noah who had a son called Shim and the later had a son called Ham who himself had a son called 'Aad,

verses.text: ٱلَّتِي لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
verses.translation: The likes of whom had never been created in the land
verses.tafsir: the like of which was not created in the land in terms of their power of assault and strength
verses.tafsirV2: (The like of which was not created in the lands) the like of their strength and height were not created in the land; it is also said that Iram is the name of a town built by Shadid and Shaddad whose columns were of gold and silver and the like of its beauty was not created in the land;

verses.text: وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُواْ ٱلصَّخۡرَ بِٱلۡوَادِ
verses.translation: And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley
verses.tafsir: and Thamūd who hollowed hewed the rocks sakhr is the plural of sakhra in the valley the Wādī al-Qurā rocks which they used as dwellings
verses.tafsirV2: (And with (the tribe of) Thamud) He says: and how He destroyed Thamud, the people of Salih, (who clove the rocks in the valley) of Qura;

verses.text: وَفِرۡعَوۡنَ ذِي ٱلۡأَوۡتَادِ
verses.translation: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes
verses.tafsir: and Pharaoh the one of the tent-pegs he used to fasten four pegs and tie to these the hands and feet of those whom he tortured —
verses.tafsirV2: (And with Pharaoh) and how He destroyed Pharaoh, (firm of right) Pharaoh erected four pillars to which he tied and tortured anyone with whom he was angry until the latter died, as he did with his wife Asiyah Bint Muzahim,

verses.text: ٱلَّذِينَ طَغَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
verses.translation: [All of] whom oppressed within the lands
verses.tafsir: those who were rebellious became tyrannical in the land
verses.tafsirV2: (Who (all) were rebellious (to Allah) in these lands) they rebelled and declared their disbelief in the land of Egypt; it is also said that their transgression led them to this,

verses.text: فَأَكۡثَرُواْ فِيهَا ٱلۡفَسَادَ
verses.translation: And increased therein the corruption
verses.tafsir: and caused much corruption therein? by way of slaying and otherwise.
verses.tafsirV2: (And multiplied iniquity) and multiplied killing innocent people and spread their idol worship (therein) in the land of Egypt?

verses.text: فَصَبَّ عَلَيۡهِمۡ رَبُّكَ سَوۡطَ عَذَابٍ
verses.translation: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment
verses.tafsir: So your Lord poured on them a scourge of chastisement.
verses.tafsirV2: (Therefore thy Lord poured on them the disaster of His punishment) your Lord sent on them a severe punishment.

verses.text: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلۡمِرۡصَادِ
verses.translation: Indeed, your Lord is in observation
verses.tafsir: Assuredly your Lord is ever on the watch watching over the deeds of servants nothing of which escapes Him that He may then requite them for these deeds.
verses.tafsirV2: (Lo! thy Lord) O Muhammad (is ever watchful) He says: they, as well as all created beings, will have to go through Him; it is also said that this means: the angels of your Lord will be on the Bridge over hell stopping people at seven different stopping positions at which they will ask them about seven traits.

verses.text: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ
verses.translation: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me
verses.tafsir: And as for man the disbeliever whenever his Lord tests him and honours him with wealth and other things and is gracious to him he says ‘My Lord has honoured me’.
verses.tafsirV2: (As for man) the disbelieving man, in reference here to Ubayy Ibn Khalaf; and it is also said: Umayyah Ibn Khalaf, (whenever his Lord trieth him) whenever his Lord tests him with wealth, richness or means of living (by honouring him) by giving him abundant wealth, (and is gracious unto him) and expands for him his means of living, (he saith: My Lord honoureth me) by giving me wealth and means of living.

verses.text: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
verses.translation: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me
verses.tafsir: But when he tests him and restricts his provision for him he says ‘My Lord has humiliated me’.
verses.tafsirV2: (But whenever He trieth him) whenever He tests him with poverty (by straitening his means of life) by tightening his means of living, (he saith: My Lord despiseth me) by giving me poverty and tightening my means of living.

verses.text: كَلَّاۖ بَل لَّا تُكۡرِمُونَ ٱلۡيَتِيمَ
verses.translation: No! But you do not honor the orphan
verses.tafsir: No indeed! — a disavowal of this notion in other words honour is not about wealth nor is there any humiliation in poverty rather it has to do with obedience and disobedience respectively; but the disbelievers of Mecca unmindful of this. Rather they do not honour the orphan they do not treat him with kindness despite their wealth or it means that they do not give him what is his due from an inheritance
verses.tafsirV2: (Nay) this is a reply to them: No, but the honour I bestow is due to My acknowledgment of some My servants and the success I give to them, while My despising is because I turn away from some servants and completely forsake them, (but ye (for your part) honour not the orphan) you do not acknowledge the right of the orphan when he is under your care.

verses.text: وَلَا تَحَـٰٓضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلۡمِسۡكِينِ
verses.translation: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor
verses.tafsir: and they do not urge neither themselves nor others the feeding of the needy;
verses.tafsirV2: (And urge not) yourselves or others (on the feeding of the poor) giving alms to the poor,

verses.text: وَتَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكۡلٗا لَّمّٗا
verses.translation: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether
verses.tafsir: and they devour inheritance turāth means mīrāth greedily lamman that is to say voraciously when they appropriate lammuhum the women’s and the young ones’ share of the inheritance together with their own share of it or to their own wealth;
verses.tafsirV2: (And ye devour heritages) inheritances (with devouring greed

verses.text: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلۡمَالَ حُبّٗا جَمّٗا
verses.translation: And you love wealth with immense love
verses.tafsir: and they love wealth with abounding love that is to say greatly and so they do not expend any of it a variant reading in the case of all four verbs has the second person plural.
verses.tafsirV2: And love wealth with abounding love.

verses.text: كَلَّآۖ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ دَكّٗا دَكّٗا
verses.translation: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed
verses.tafsir: No indeed! — a deterrent for them from such conduct. When the earth is pulverised repeatedly when it is shaken until every edifice has collapsed and is destroyed
verses.tafsirV2: Nay) this is also a reply to them, (but when the earth is ground to atoms, grinding, grinding) He says: when the earth is quaked again and again,

verses.text: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفّٗا صَفّٗا
verses.translation: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank
verses.tafsir: and your Lord that is to say His command and the angels arrive rank on rank saffan saffan is a circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘standing in rows’ or ‘made up of many ranks’
verses.tafsirV2: (And thy Lord shall come) a coming without any modality (with angels, rank on rank) like the ranks of the people of the life of the world when praying,

verses.text: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذٖ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
verses.translation: And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but what good to him will be the remembrance
verses.tafsir: and Hell on that day is brought near pulled by seventy thousand sets of reins each set of reins pulled by the hands of seventy thousand angels as it groans and seethes in fury; on that day yawma’idhin is a substitution for idhā ‘when’ the response to which is the following man that is to say the disbeliever will remember his prodigal conduct in it but how will remembering avail him now? the interrogative is meant as a denial in other words his remembering that will not be of any use to him.
verses.tafsirV2: (And hell is brought near) with 70,000 registers, with each register 70,000 angels leading it to the place of mustering, and then they reveal them (that day) the Day of Judgement; (on that day man) the disbelieving man; i.e. Ubayy Ibn Khalaf and Umayyah Ibn Khalaf (will remember) will be admonished, (but how will the remembrance (then avail him)) when the time for being admonished has passed?

verses.text: يَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي قَدَّمۡتُ لِحَيَاتِي
verses.translation: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life
verses.tafsir: He will say as he remembers ‘O yā is for calling attention to something would that I had sent ahead good deeds and faith for my life!’ for a good life in the Hereafter or it means ‘during my life’ in the world.
verses.tafsirV2: (He will say: Ah, would that) wishing: if only (I had sent before me (some provision) for my life!) if only I have worked in my previous perishing life to this everlasting life.

verses.text: فَيَوۡمَئِذٖ لَّا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُۥٓ أَحَدٞ
verses.translation: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment
verses.tafsir: Then on that day none shall mete out read yu‘adhdhibu His God’s chastisement that is to say He shall not delegate it to any other;
verses.tafsirV2: (None punisheth as He will punish on that day) on the Day of Judgement!

verses.text: وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُۥٓ أَحَدٞ
verses.translation: And none will bind [as severely] as His binding [of the evildoers]
verses.tafsir: and likewise none shall bind read yūthiqu His bind a variant reading has yu‘adhdhabu ‘none shall be chastised’ and yūthaqu ‘none shall be bound’ so that the suffixed pronoun of ‘adhābahu and wathāqahu refers to the chastisement and the binds of the disbeliever the meaning then being ‘none shall be chastised as he shall and none shall be bound as he shall be bound’.
verses.tafsirV2: (None bindeth as He then will bind) this can also be understood to mean: none punishes like this and none will inflict that kind of punishment except Allah.

verses.text: يَـٰٓأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفۡسُ ٱلۡمُطۡمَئِنَّةُ
verses.translation: [To the righteous it will be said], "O reassured soul
verses.tafsir: ‘O soul at peace! the one secure namely the believing one.
verses.tafsirV2: (But ah! thou soul at peace) which is safe from Allah's chastisement, true in its profession of Allah's divine Oneness, grateful for the blessings Allah bestowed upon it, patient with the trials of Allah, pleased with things decreed by Allah, and content with that which Allah gives!

verses.text: ٱرۡجِعِيٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةٗ مَّرۡضِيَّةٗ
verses.translation: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]
verses.tafsir: Return — this is said to it upon death — to your Lord that is to say return to His command and to His will pleased with the reward pleasing in God’s sight with your deeds; in other words return O soul combining both descriptions both of which are circumstantial qualifiers. And it will be said to it at the Resurrection
verses.tafsirV2: (Return unto thy Lord) return to that which Allah has prepared for you in the Garden; and it is also said this means: return to your master: the body, (content) with Allah's reward (in His good pleasure) because of its belief in Allah's divine Oneness!

verses.text: فَٱدۡخُلِي فِي عِبَٰدِي
verses.translation: And enter among My [righteous] servants
verses.tafsir: Then enter among My righteous servants!
verses.tafsirV2: (Enter thou among My bondmen) enter you among My friends!

verses.text: وَٱدۡخُلِي جَنَّتِي
verses.translation: And enter My Paradise
verses.tafsir: And enter My Paradise!’ with them.
verses.tafsirV2: (Enter thou My Garden) which I have prepared for you!'

verses.text: لَآ أُقۡسِمُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡبَلَدِ
verses.translation: I swear by this city, Makkah
verses.tafsir: I swear lā is extra by this land of Mecca
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Nay, I swear by this city): '(Nay, I swear by this city) He says: I swear by the city of Mecca

verses.text: وَأَنتَ حِلُّۢ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡبَلَدِ
verses.translation: And you, [O Muhammad], are free of restriction in this city
verses.tafsir: and you O Muhammad (s) have free disposal of sanction for this land in that you will be given permission to fight in it — and indeed God fulfilled this promise to him on the day of the Conquest of Mecca thus this is a parenthetical statement intervening between that by which the oath has been sworn and that which is a supplement thereto.
verses.tafsirV2: (And thou art an indweller of this city) and it is also said that this means: Allah has made lawful for you in this city that which he did not make lawful to anyone before or after you; and it is also said that this means: you are excused regarding that which you do in this city.

verses.text: وَوَالِدٖ وَمَا وَلَدَ
verses.translation: And [by] the father and that which was born [of him]
verses.tafsir: And by the begetter that is Adam and that which he begat that is his descendants mā ‘that which’ actually means man ‘whom’.
verses.tafsirV2: (And the begetter and that which he begat) the begetter is Adam and that which his sons begat; and it is also said this means: the begetter refers to the person who can have children, whether this person is a man or a woman, while that which he begat refers to the men or women who cannot have children; Allah swore by all these,

verses.text: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِي كَبَدٍ
verses.translation: We have certainly created man into hardship
verses.tafsir: We certainly created man al-insān the generic noun in travail in a state of toil and hardship struggling with the tribulations of this world and the calamities of the Hereafter.
verses.tafsirV2: (We verily have created man) i.e. Kildah Ibn Usayd (in an atmosphere) in an erect form; it is also said that this means: in strife with the matter of the life of this world and of the Hereafter; and it is also said this means: with strength and force:

verses.text: أَيَحۡسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ أَحَدٞ
verses.translation: Does he think that never will anyone overcome him
verses.tafsir: Does he suppose does the strong man of Quraysh namely Abū’l-Ashadd b. Kalada presume on account of his strength that an softened in place of the hardened form its subject omitted that is to say annahu no one will have power over him? Yet God has power over him.
verses.tafsirV2: (Thinketh he) does the disbelieving man think (that) because of his strength and force (none hath power over him?) i.e. Allah cannot seize and punish him.

verses.text: يَقُولُ أَهۡلَكۡتُ مَالٗا لُّبَدًا
verses.translation: He says, "I have spent wealth in abundance
verses.tafsir: He says ‘I have exhausted in enmity of Muhammad (s) vast wealth!’ great wealth piles and piles of it.
verses.tafsirV2: (And he) Kildah Ibn Usayd; and it is also said: al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah (saith: I have destroyed vast wealth) I have spent abundant wealth in enmity towards Muhammad, Allah bless him, and this did not benefit me:

verses.text: أَيَحۡسَبُ أَن لَّمۡ يَرَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ
verses.translation: Does he think that no one has seen him
verses.tafsir: Does he suppose that an in other words annahu no one has seen him? with regard to what he has expended to know the quantity thereof; God knows the quantity thereof; but it is not in reality that much so as to be considered a great amount and in any case He will requite him for his evil conduct.
verses.tafsirV2: (Thinketh he) does the disbelieving man deem (that none beholdeth him) that Allah does not see his deeds whether he spends money or not?

verses.text: أَلَمۡ نَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ عَيۡنَيۡنِ
verses.translation: Have We not made for him two eyes
verses.tafsir: Have We not given an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words ‘We have certainly given’ him two eyes
verses.tafsirV2: Allah then mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon him, saying: (Did We not assign unto him two eyes) with which he sees

verses.text: وَلِسَانٗا وَشَفَتَيۡنِ
verses.translation: And a tongue and two lips
verses.tafsir: and a tongue and two lips
verses.tafsirV2: (And a tongue) with which he speaks (and two lips) which he can join together or separate,

verses.text: وَهَدَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلنَّجۡدَيۡنِ
verses.translation: And have shown him the two ways
verses.tafsir: and guided him to the two paths? did We not point out to him the path of good and that of evil?
verses.tafsirV2: (And guide him to the parting of the mountain ways?) And We showed him the way of goodness and the way of evil; and it is also that this means: the way to the two breasts.

verses.text: فَلَا ٱقۡتَحَمَ ٱلۡعَقَبَةَ
verses.translation: But he has not broken through the difficult pass
verses.tafsir: Yet why does he not assault the obstacle? why does he not surmount it?
verses.tafsirV2: (But he hath not attempted the Ascent) He says: but did he go beyond that hurdle which is the Bridge over hell?

verses.text: وَمَآ أَدۡرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلۡعَقَبَةُ
verses.translation: And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass
verses.tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you what the obstacle is? that he is to surmount — intended to emphasise its enormity this statement is a parenthetical one. He explains the way to surmount it by saying
verses.tafsirV2: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Ascent is!) it is a smooth hurdle between Paradise and hell. Allah said this to arouse the Prophet's astonishment.

verses.text: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ
verses.translation: It is the freeing of a slave
verses.tafsir: the freeing of a slave from bondage
verses.tafsirV2: ((It is) to free a slave) He says: its crossing requires the freeing of a slave; and it is also said this means: none will cross it save he who has freed a slave,

verses.text: أَوۡ إِطۡعَٰمٞ فِي يَوۡمٖ ذِي مَسۡغَبَةٖ
verses.translation: Or feeding on a day of severe hunger
verses.tafsir: or to give food on a day of hunger
verses.tafsirV2: (And to feed in the day of hunger) and hardship

verses.text: يَتِيمٗا ذَا مَقۡرَبَةٍ
verses.translation: An orphan of near relationship
verses.tafsir: to an orphan near of kin maqraba means qarāba
verses.tafsirV2: (An orphan near of kin,

verses.text: أَوۡ مِسۡكِينٗا ذَا مَتۡرَبَةٖ
verses.translation: Or a needy person in misery
verses.tafsir: or a needy person in misery matraba literally means ‘clinging to the dust turāb’ because of his poverty; a variant reading has two verbal nouns in place of the two verbs fakka ‘he freed’ and at‘ama ‘he fed’ the first being in a genitive construction fakku raqabatin ‘the freeing of a slave’ and the second with nunation it‘āmun ‘to give food’ in which case there is an implied iqtihāmu before al-‘aqaba of which the said reading becomes the explication;
verses.tafsirV2: Or some poor wretch in misery) and who has nothing,

verses.text: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡمَرۡحَمَةِ
verses.translation: And then being among those who believed and advised one another to patience and advised one another to compassion
verses.tafsir: while being thumma kāna is a supplement to iqtahama ‘he assaulted’; thumma is for the ordering of things to be mentioned in other words what is meant is that at the point of the assault he was one of those who believe and enjoin one another to steadfastness in pursuing obedience and in refraining from disobedience and enjoin one another to compassion marhama means rahma towards creatures.
verses.tafsirV2: (And to be) in addition to this (of those who believe) in private between themselves and their Lord, in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and exhort one another to perseverance) in fulfilling the obligations (and export one another to pity) towards the poor and needy.

verses.text: أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡمَيۡمَنَةِ
verses.translation: Those are the companions of the right
verses.tafsir: Those the ones described by the said attributes are the ones of the right side al-maymana means al-yamīn.
verses.tafsirV2: (Their place will be on the right hand) those who are given their register in their right hands are the inhabitants of the Garden.

verses.text: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا هُمۡ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡمَشۡـَٔمَةِ
verses.translation: But they who disbelieved in Our signs - those are the companions of the left
verses.tafsir: But those who disbelieve in Our signs they are the ones of the left side al-mash’ama means al-shimāl.
verses.tafsirV2: (But those who disbelieve Our revelations) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, i.e. Kildah and his host, (their place will be on the left hand) those who are given their register in their left hand are the inhabitants of the Fire.

verses.text: عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَارٞ مُّؤۡصَدَةُۢ
verses.translation: Over them will be fire closed in
verses.tafsir: Over them will be an enclosing Fire read mu’sada or mūsada closed on top of them.
verses.tafsirV2: (Fire will be an awning over them) the Fire will fall on them'.

verses.text: وَٱلشَّمۡسِ وَضُحَىٰهَا
verses.translation: By the sun and its brightness
verses.tafsir: By the sun and her morning light
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the sun and his brightness): '(By the sun and his brightness) Allah swears by the sun and its light,

verses.text: وَٱلۡقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَىٰهَا
verses.translation: And [by] the moon when it follows it
verses.tafsir: and by the moon when it follows her rising after she has set
verses.tafsirV2: (And the moon when she followeth him) when it follows the sun, on the first night when the new moon is seen,

verses.text: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلَّىٰهَا
verses.translation: And [by] the day when it displays it
verses.tafsir: and by the day when it reveals her as it rises high
verses.tafsirV2: (And the day when it revealeth him,

verses.text: وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَغۡشَىٰهَا
verses.translation: And [by] the night when it covers it
verses.tafsir: and by the night when it enshrouds her covering her up with its darkness idhā ‘when’ in all three instances is an absolute adverbial operated by the verbal action of the oath.
verses.tafsirV2: And the night when it enshroudeth him) and the night when it enshrouds the light of day and the day reveals the darkness of the night,

verses.text: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا بَنَىٰهَا
verses.translation: And [by] the sky and He who constructed it
verses.tafsir: By the heaven and the One Who built it
verses.tafsirV2: (And the heaven and Him who built it) by Him Who created it, i.e. Allah, Allah swore by Himself,

verses.text: وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا طَحَىٰهَا
verses.translation: And [by] the earth and He who spread it
verses.tafsir: and by the earth and the One Who spread it laid out flat.
verses.tafsirV2: (And the earth and Him who spread it) over the water,

verses.text: وَنَفۡسٖ وَمَا سَوَّىٰهَا
verses.translation: And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it
verses.tafsir: and by the soul that is to say by all souls and the One Who proportioned it in its created form mā in all three instances relates to the verbal action or functions as man ‘the one who’
verses.tafsirV2: (And a soul and Him who perfected it) by creating it with two hands, two feet, two eyes, two ears as well as with all the other organs.

verses.text: فَأَلۡهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقۡوَىٰهَا
verses.translation: And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness
verses.tafsir: and inspired to discern its vices and piety He pointed out to it the path of good and that of evil the placing of taqwā ‘piety’ second takes into account the rhyme endings of the verses; the response to the oath is the following
verses.tafsirV2: (And inspired it (with conscience of) what is wrong for it and (what is) right for it) He made known to it and explained what it should go for and what it should avoid; Allah swore by all these things as well as by Himself.

verses.text: قَدۡ أَفۡلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا
verses.translation: He has succeeded who purifies it
verses.tafsir: Successful indeed qad the lām of laqad ‘indeed’ has been omitted from it for the sake of brevity will be the one who purifies it purges it of sins
verses.tafsirV2: (He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow) who refines it, makes things clear for it and guides it to success,

verses.text: وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا
verses.translation: And he has failed who instills it [with corruption]
verses.tafsir: and he will indeed have failed he who eclipses it he who obscures it with acts of disobedience dassāhā is actually dassasahā but the second sīn has been replaced with an alif for phonetic ease.
verses.tafsirV2: (And he is indeed a failure) he is in loss (who stunteth it) who leads to sin, error and forsakenness.

verses.text: كَذَّبَتۡ ثَمُودُ بِطَغۡوَىٰهَآ
verses.translation: Thamud denied [their prophet] by reason of their transgression
verses.tafsir: Thamūd denied their messenger Sālih because of their rebellious nature
verses.tafsirV2: (The tribe of) Thamud) the folk of Salih (denied (the Truth) in their rebellious pride) He says: their transgression led them to this.

verses.text: إِذِ ٱنۢبَعَثَ أَشۡقَىٰهَا
verses.translation: When the most wretched of them was sent forth
verses.tafsir: when the most wretched of them whose name was Qudār was dispatched when he hastened in order to hamstring the she-camel with their approval.
verses.tafsirV2: (When the basest of them broke forth) when the most wretched of the folk, Qudar Ibn Salif and Masda', hamstrung the she-camel.

verses.text: فَقَالَ لَهُمۡ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقۡيَٰهَا
verses.translation: And the messenger of Allah [Salih] said to them, "[Do not harm] the she-camel of Allah or [prevent her from] her drink
verses.tafsir: But then the messenger of God Sālih said to them ‘This is the she-camel of God so let her have her drink!’ her drink on her day — one day was hers the next theirs.
verses.tafsirV2: (And the messenger of Allah) Salih (said) that is before they hamstrung the she-camel: (It is the she-camel of Allah) leave the she-camel of Allah alone, (so let her drink!) i.e. and let her drink in peace!

verses.text: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمۡدَمَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ رَبُّهُم بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ فَسَوَّىٰهَا
verses.translation: But they denied him and hamstrung her. So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and made it equal [upon all of them]
verses.tafsir: But they denied him with regard to his saying this as being a command from God — which if they contravened would immediately result in chastisement being sent down on them — then hamstrung her they slew it in order to appropriate her share of the drinking water. So their Lord closed in on them the chastisement because of their sin and meted it equally among them that is the closing in on them in other words He subsumed them all by it so that not one of them escaped.
verses.tafsirV2: (But they denied him) they denied the message brought by Salih, (and they hamstrung her) they hamstrung the she-camel, (so Allah doomed them for their sin) so Allah destroyed them because of killing the she-camel and disbelieving in Salih (and razed (their dwellings)) killing the old and the young among them.

verses.text: وَلَا يَخَافُ عُقۡبَٰهَا
verses.translation: And He does not fear the consequence thereof
verses.tafsir: And He does not read wa-lā or fa-lā fear the consequence of it.
verses.tafsirV2: (He dreadeth not the sequel (of events)) and it is also said this means: and He dreads not the one who instigated it'.

verses.text: وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَغۡشَىٰ
verses.translation: By the night when it covers
verses.tafsir: By the night as it enshrouds with its darkness all that is between the heaven and the earth
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying: (By the night enshrouding): '(By the night enshrouding) He says: Allah swears by the night when it enshrouds the light of day.

verses.text: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ
verses.translation: And [by] the day when it appears
verses.tafsir: and by the day as it unveils as it is revealed and becomes manifest idhā ‘as’ in both instances is an absolute adverbial operated by the verbal action of the oath
verses.tafsirV2: (And the day resplendent) and the day when it clears the darkness of night.

verses.text: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰٓ
verses.translation: And [by] He who created the male and female
verses.tafsir: and by the One Who mā either functions as man ‘the One Who’ or it is related to a verbal action created the male and the female Adam and Eve or every male and female — the hermaphrodite although problematic for us is in fact either male or female according to God and therefore a person actually commits perjury if he speaks with one thinking that because he has sworn not to speak with a male or a female; he may do so with a hermaphrodite.
verses.tafsirV2: (And Him Who hath created) and by Him Who has created the (male and female,

verses.text: إِنَّ سَعۡيَكُمۡ لَشَتَّىٰ
verses.translation: Indeed, your efforts are diverse
verses.tafsir: Assuredly your efforts your deeds are dissimilar with some working towards Paradise by means of obedience while others in effect are working towards the Fire through acts of disobedience.
verses.tafsirV2: Lo! your effort) your work (is dispersed (towards diverse ends)) there are those who oppose and disbelieve in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an and there are those who believe in Muhammad (pbuh); there are those who strive for Paradise and there are those who strive for hell. This is why Allah made the oath.

verses.text: فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أَعۡطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ
verses.translation: As for he who gives and fears Allah
verses.tafsir: As for him who gives what is due to God and is fearful of God
verses.tafsirV2: (As for him who giveth) to charity from his wealth for the sake of Allah and bought nine believers who were in the hands of the disbelievers who tortured them to renounce their religion; this person bought them and then freed them (and is dutiful (towards Allah)) and wards off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies

verses.text: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ
verses.translation: And believes in the best [reward]
verses.tafsir: and affirms the truth of the best word that is the truth of ‘there is no god but God’ in both places here and below verse 9
verses.tafsirV2: (And believeth in goodness) and believes in Allah's provision; and it is also said this means: and believes in Paradise; and it is also said this means: and believes in " there is no deity save Allah " ;

verses.text: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلۡيُسۡرَىٰ
verses.translation: We will ease him toward ease
verses.tafsir: We shall surely ease his way to the abode of ease to Paradise.
verses.tafsirV2: (Surely We will ease his way unto the state of ease) We shall make easy for him acts of obedience and give him success, time and again, to perform acts of obedience; and it is also said this means: We shall give him success, time and again, to give alms for the sake of Allah; this refers to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

verses.text: وَأَمَّا مَنۢ بَخِلَ وَٱسۡتَغۡنَىٰ
verses.translation: But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need
verses.tafsir: But as for him who is niggardly with what is due to God and deems himself self-sufficient without need for His reward 929 and denies the best word
verses.tafsirV2: (But as for him who hoardeth) his wealth and is too stingy to give for the sake of Allah, in reference here to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah and it is said: Abu Sufyan Ibn Harb who was not a believer at that time (and deemeth himself independent) of Allah,

verses.text: وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ
verses.translation: And denies the best [reward]
verses.tafsir: and denies the best word
verses.tafsirV2: (And disbelieveth in goodness) and disbelieves in Allah's provision; and it is also said: in Paradise; and it is also said: in " there is no deity save Allah " ;

verses.text: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلۡعُسۡرَىٰ
verses.translation: We will ease him toward difficulty
verses.tafsir: We shall surely ease his way We shall pave for him the way to hardship to the Fire;
verses.tafsirV2: (Surely We will ease his way unto adversity) We shall make easy for him acts of disobedience and refraining from giving to charity, time and again.

verses.text: وَمَا يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُ مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ
verses.translation: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls
verses.tafsir: And his wealth shall not mā is or negation avail him when he perishes in the Fire.
verses.tafsirV2: (His riches) which he amasses in the life of the world (will not save him when he perisheth) when he dies; and it is also said this means: when he is cast in the Fire.

verses.text: إِنَّ عَلَيۡنَا لَلۡهُدَىٰ
verses.translation: Indeed, [incumbent] upon Us is guidance
verses.tafsir: Truly with Us lies all guidance the pointing out of the path of guidance from that of error so that Our command may be followed by adhering to the former manner of conduct and that Our prohibition may also be heeded by refraining from falling into the latter manner of conduct.
verses.tafsirV2: (Lo! Ours it is (to give) the guidance) it is for Us to show what is good and what is evil

verses.text: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلۡأٓخِرَةَ وَٱلۡأُولَىٰ
verses.translation: And indeed, to Us belongs the Hereafter and the first [life]
verses.tafsir: And truly to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life that is to say that of this world and so whoever seeks either of the two from anyone other than Us has erred.
verses.tafsirV2: (And lo! unto Us belong the latter portion and the former) and to Us belong the reward of the life of the world and that of the Hereafter; it is also said that this means: to Us belong the life of the world in which We bestow knowledge and success and also the Hereafter in which We bestow reward and honour.

verses.text: فَأَنذَرۡتُكُمۡ نَارٗا تَلَظَّىٰ
verses.translation: So I have warned you of a Fire which is blazing
verses.tafsir: So I have warned you of I have threatened you O people of Mecca with a raging fire talazzā ‘raging’ one of the two original tā’ letters of tatalazzā has been omitted; a variant reading retains it tatalazzā that is ‘one that is flaming’
verses.tafsirV2: (Therefore have I warned you) of people of Mecca by means of the Qur'an (of the flaming Fire

verses.text: لَا يَصۡلَىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلۡأَشۡقَى
verses.translation: None will [enter to] burn therein except the most wretched one
verses.tafsir: which none shall enter but the wretched one al-ashqā means al-shaqī
verses.tafsirV2: Which only the most wretched must endure) which only the wretched, as in Allah's foreknowledge, will enter,

verses.text: ٱلَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
verses.translation: Who had denied and turned away
verses.tafsir: he who denies the Prophet and turns away from faith — this delimiting of those who deserve to enter this fire constitutes an interpretation of His saying But He forgives other than that to whomever He will Q. 448 which in turn suggests that what is meant is that entry into the Fire which will be everlasting.
verses.tafsirV2: (He who denieth) Allah's divine Oneness; and it is also said: who falls short in obeying Allah (and turneth away) from faith; and it is also said: from repentance.

verses.text: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلۡأَتۡقَى
verses.translation: But the righteous one will avoid it
verses.tafsir: The God-fearing one al-atqā means al-taqī shall be spared it he will be removed far away from it
verses.tafsirV2: (Far removed from it) from the Fire (will be the righteous

verses.text: ٱلَّذِي يُؤۡتِي مَالَهُۥ يَتَزَكَّىٰ
verses.translation: [He] who gives [from] his wealth to purify himself
verses.tafsir: he who gives his wealth to purify himself offering it as a means of self purification before God exalted be He by making this payment for the sake of God exalted be He and not for show or the sake of reputation so that he or the offering stands purified in the sight of God. This verse was revealed regarding the truthful one al-siddīq Abū Bakr may God be pleased with him when he purchased Bilāl the Ethiopian who was being tortured on account of his faith and then freed him whereat the disbelievers said ‘He only did this in return for a favour which he must have owed him’ and so the following was revealed
verses.tafsirV2: Who giveth his wealth) in the way of Allah, i.e. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (that he may grow (in goodness)) intending by that Allah's Countenance alone,

verses.text: وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعۡمَةٖ تُجۡزَىٰٓ
verses.translation: And not [giving] for anyone who has [done him] a favor to be rewarded
verses.tafsir: and no one has any favour outstanding with him that must be requited;
verses.tafsirV2: (And none hath with him any favour for reward,

verses.text: إِلَّا ٱبۡتِغَآءَ وَجۡهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ
verses.translation: But only seeking the countenance of his Lord, Most High
verses.tafsir: but he did this only seeking the pleasure of his Lord the Most High that is to say only seeking to secure God’s reward;
verses.tafsirV2: Except as seeking (to fulfil) the purpose of his Lord Most High) except seeking the good pleasure of his Lord the Most High, Who is higher than everything.

verses.text: وَلَسَوۡفَ يَرۡضَىٰ
verses.translation: And he is going to be satisfied
verses.tafsir: and verily soon he shall himself be pleased with the reward he will be given in Paradise. The verse applies equally to anyone who may do as he Abū Bakr did may God be pleased with him and such a person will thereby be removed far from the Fire and rewarded.
verses.tafsirV2: (He verily will be content) he will be given of reward and honour until he is pleased, i.e. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his fellow believers'.

verses.text: وَٱلضُّحَىٰ
verses.translation: By the morning brightness
verses.tafsir: By the forenoon that is to say the first part of the day or all of it
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the morning hours): '(By the morning hours) He says: Allah swears by the whole day

verses.text: وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ
verses.translation: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
verses.tafsir: and by the night when it is still — or sajā can mean ‘when it envelops all in its darkness’.
verses.tafsirV2: (And by the night when it is stillest) and by the night when it becomes dark,

verses.text: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ
verses.translation: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, [O Muhammad], nor has He detested [you]
verses.tafsir: Your Lord has neither forsaken you He has not abandoned you O Muhammad (s) nor does He hate you this was revealed when after the revelation had not come to him for fifteen days the disbelievers said ‘His Lord has parted with him and hates him’.
verses.tafsirV2: (Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee) your Lord has not left you since He inspired you (nor doth He hate thee) since He loved you; this is the reason for Allah's oath, this was revealed after the revelations from Allah stopped for 15 nights because the Prophet (pbuh) forgot to say " if Allah wills " when he promised the idolaters to answer their questions. And because the revelations stopped for this period of time the idolaters said: the Lord of Prophet has forsaken him and He hates him.

verses.text: وَلَلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرٞ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ
verses.translation: And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life]
verses.tafsir: And verily the Hereafter shall be better for you by virtue of the honours awaiting you thereat than the first life this world.
verses.tafsirV2: (And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former) He says: the reward of the Hereafter is better for you than the reward of the life of the world.

verses.text: وَلَسَوۡفَ يُعۡطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرۡضَىٰٓ
verses.translation: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied
verses.tafsir: And verily your Lord shall give you in the Hereafter of good things a bounteous gift and you shall be satisfied with it — and so the Prophet s said ‘In that case I shall not be satisfied if a single person from among my community remains in the Fire’ the response to the oath terminates here with two affirmations and two negations.
verses.tafsirV2: (And verily thy Lord will give unto thee) in the Hereafter of intercession (so that thou wilt be content) until you are content.

verses.text: أَلَمۡ يَجِدۡكَ يَتِيمٗا فَـَٔاوَىٰ
verses.translation: Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge
verses.tafsir: Did He not find you an orphan an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words He did indeed find you an orphan having lost your father before you were born or shortly thereafter and shelter you? by having your uncle Abū Tālib embrace you as part of his household.
verses.tafsirV2: Allah then mentioned His blessings upon the Prophet (pbuh) saying (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (an orphan) without a father or mother (and protect (thee)) and joined you to your uncle Abu Talib and sufficed you your provision? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

verses.text: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلّٗا فَهَدَىٰ
verses.translation: And He found you lost and guided [you]
verses.tafsir: And did He not find you erring from the revealed Law which you now follow and guided you? that is and then guided you to it.
verses.tafsirV2: Gabriel then said: (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (wandering) among people in error (and direct (thee)) and guided you by means of prophethood? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

verses.text: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلٗا فَأَغۡنَىٰ
verses.translation: And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient
verses.tafsir: And did He not find you needy poor and enrich you? and made you content with the spoils and other things which He gave you — in a hadīth it is stated ‘Wealth comes not from the proliferation of transient worldly goods but wealth comes from the contentedness of the soul’.
verses.tafsirV2: And he also said: (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (destitute) poor (and enrich (thee)) with the wealth of Khadijah; and it is also said this means: and made you content with that which He gave you? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

verses.text: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقۡهَرۡ
verses.translation: So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]
verses.tafsir: So as for the orphan do not oppress him by appropriating his wealth or otherwise
verses.tafsirV2: So he also said: (Therefore the orphan oppress not) do not transgress on him nor deride him,

verses.text: وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنۡهَرۡ
verses.translation: And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him]
verses.tafsir: and as for the beggar do not drive him away do not repel him on account of his poverty
verses.tafsirV2: (Therefore the beggar drive not away) nor rebuke,

verses.text: وَأَمَّا بِنِعۡمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثۡ
verses.translation: But as for the favor of your Lord, report [it]
verses.tafsir: and as for your Lord’s grace to you by way of prophethood and otherwise proclaim it make it known. The omission in certain instances of the suffixed pronoun referring to the Prophet s from the end of the verbs is intended to sustain the end-rhyme of the verses.
verses.tafsirV2: (Therefore of the bounty of thy Lord) through prophethood and Islam (be thy discourse) speak to people and let them know about it'.

verses.text: أَلَمۡ نَشۡرَحۡ لَكَ صَدۡرَكَ
verses.translation: Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast
verses.tafsir: Did We not expand an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words ‘We did indeed expand’ your breast for you O Muhammad (s) by means of prophethood and otherwise
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate): '(Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate) this is in conjunction with His saying (Did He not find thee destitute and enrich (thee)?), and so Allah says: did We not open your heart for Islam? i.e. did We not soften your heart on the Day of the Covenant through knowledge, understanding, help, reason and certainty, as well as with other things? It is also said this means: did We not expand your heart through prophethood? And the Prophet (pbuh) said: “Yes, indeed!”

verses.text: وَوَضَعۡنَا عَنكَ وِزۡرَكَ
verses.translation: And We removed from you your burden
verses.tafsir: and relieve you of your burden
verses.tafsirV2: He said again: (And eased thee of the burden) We lifted your sins from you

verses.text: ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنقَضَ ظَهۡرَكَ
verses.translation: Which had weighed upon your back
verses.tafsir: that which weighed down your back? — this is similar to where God says that God may forgive you what is past of your sin Q. 482.
verses.tafsirV2: (Which weighed down thy back?) It is also said: prophethood weighed down your back; And the Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, indeed! "

verses.text: وَرَفَعۡنَا لَكَ ذِكۡرَكَ
verses.translation: And raised high for you your repute
verses.tafsir: Did We not exalt your mention? For you are mentioned where I God am mentioned in the call announcing the time for prayer adhān in the second call to perform the prayer iqāma in the witnessing ‘there is no god but God Muhammad is His Messenger’ tashahhud in the Friday sermon and in other instances.
verses.tafsirV2: (And exalted thy fame) and raised your voice with the call to prayer, supplication and testification of faith, such that you are mentioned just as I am? And the Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, indeed! "

verses.text: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلۡعُسۡرِ يُسۡرًا
verses.translation: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease
verses.tafsir: For truly with hardship comes ease.
verses.tafsirV2: Allah then said to comfort His prophet about his poverty and the hardships he faced, saying: (But lo! with hardship goeth ease,

verses.text: إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلۡعُسۡرِ يُسۡرٗا
verses.translation: Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease
verses.tafsir: Truly with hardship comes ease the Prophet s suffered much hardship at the hands of the disbelievers but then he enjoyed ease when he was assisted to victory by God over them.
verses.tafsirV2: Lo! with hardship goeth ease;

verses.text: فَإِذَا فَرَغۡتَ فَٱنصَبۡ
verses.translation: So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship]
verses.tafsir: So when you are finished from performing prayer toil exert yourself in supplication to God
verses.tafsirV2: So when thou art relieved) when you finish from military expeditions, jihad and fighting, (still toil) in worship; and it is also said this means: when you finish from the prescribed prayers, make supplications

verses.text: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرۡغَب
verses.translation: And to your Lord direct [your] longing
verses.tafsir: and seek devote yourself humbly to your Lord.
verses.tafsirV2: (And strive to please thy Lord) and ask your needs from your Lord'.

verses.text: وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونِ
verses.translation: By the fig and the olive
verses.tafsir: By the fig and the olive that is the two edible foods — or these denote the names of two mountains in Syria on which these two foods grow —
verses.tafsirV2: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the fig and the olive): '(By the fig and the olive) He says: Allah swears by the fig, this fig of yours, and the olive, this olive of yours; it is also said the fig and the olive refer to two mountains in Historic Syria; it is also said that the fig refers to the hill upon which Jerusalem is built while the olive refers to the mountain upon which Damascus is built,

verses.text: وَطُورِ سِينِينَ
verses.translation: And [by] Mount Sinai
verses.tafsir: and by the Mount Sinai the mountain on which God exalted be He spoke to Moses sīnīn means ‘the one blessed’ or ‘the fair one with fruitful trees’
verses.tafsirV2: (By Mount Sinai) and He swears by the mountain of Thubayr which is the mountain of Midian where Allah spoke to Moses (pbuh),

verses.text: وَهَٰذَا ٱلۡبَلَدِ ٱلۡأَمِينِ
verses.translation: And [by] this secure city [Makkah]
verses.tafsir: and by this secure land Mecca as people were secure in it in the time of pagandom and are still secure in it in Islam.
verses.tafsirV2: (And by this land made safe) and He swears by Mecca which is made safe in that whoever enters it is safe;

verses.text: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِيٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٖ
verses.translation: We have certainly created man in the best of stature
verses.tafsir: Verily We created man al-insān the generic in the best of forms in the best proportioning of his shape.
